solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Sickly old man’s turkey in need of stuffing (5)

indicators.note: the turkey has lost its stuffing, so only its shell of first and last letters is left

blocks.note: pa = father, the old man; with the 's
TURKEY with its insides (URKE) removed

annotation.surface: A pale, poorly father whose Christmas turkey has not yet been stuffed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stuffing' looks like part of the cooking, but it means the turkey's inside letters, which are missing.
annotation.definitionFit: A pasty complexion is pale and unhealthy-looking, so pasty means sickly.

entries.clue: Copper and phosphorus found above abandoned coalmine (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the next
wild, uncontrolled: the letters of COALMINE are let loose

blocks.note: P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus
the letters of COALMINE rearranged

annotation.surface: A chemistry note: copper and phosphorus deposits discovered above a disused coal pit.
annotation.walkthrough: With 'phosphorus' beside it, 'Copper' reads as the metal Cu; it is the slang for a police officer.
annotation.definitionFit: Copper is everyday slang for a police officer.

entries.clue: More cunning hitman killing fifth of Mafia (5)

indicators.note: the hitman does away with a letter

blocks.note: a slayer is a killer
the fifth letter of MAFIA, taken out of SLAYER

annotation.surface: A crafty contract killer who bumps off a fifth of the Mafia.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fifth of Mafia' is not a fraction of the gang but its fifth letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Slyer is the comparative of sly, so it means more cunning.

entries.clue: Abridged long stories for almanacs (8)

indicators.note: shortened: YEARN loses its last letter

blocks.note: to long = to YEARN, cut short
stories = fibs, lies

annotation.surface: Almanacs that condense long tales into shorter versions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing the stories; it is the verb to yearn.
annotation.definitionFit: A yearly is a publication issued once a year, as an almanac is.

entries.clue: Spooner’s fruitcake could earn extra dosh (9)

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner swapped the first sounds of words

blocks.note: fruitcake = loon, a crazy person; it takes the M from the next word
could = might; it takes the L from the first word

annotation.surface: A fruitcake so good that selling it could make you some extra cash.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fruitcake' is slang for an eccentric, not the bake. Moonlighting is taking a second job, often on the quiet.
annotation.definitionFit: To moonlight is to take a second job for extra money; dosh is British slang for cash.

entries.clue: One cloud over south of France (4)

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned over: read from the bottom up

blocks.note: I = one, the Roman numeral
to cloud = to dim, as a mood or a glass is clouded

annotation.surface: A single cloud drifting over the south of France.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cloud' looks like a noun in a weather report; it is the verb to dim. I then DIM, read upwards, gives the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: French for midday, Midi is also the French name for the southern region, where the noon sun lies.

entries.clue: Sole Briton performing in three-star line-up (6,4)

indicators.note: the letters put on an act in a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: The only British act in a line-up of three star performers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Three-star' suggests a hotel or a celebrity bill; the stars are real ones in the sky.
annotation.definitionFit: Orion's Belt is the short straight row of three bright stars in the constellation Orion.

entries.clue: Can’t abide old tool boxes (6)

indicators.note: puts in a box: LATHE encloses O

blocks.note: a lathe is a machine tool for turning wood or metal; it wraps round the O
O is the abbreviation for old

annotation.surface: Someone who cannot stand old-fashioned tool boxes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tool boxes' reads as one noun, a toolbox; split it, and 'boxes' is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: hating something so much you cannot put up with it.

entries.clue: Birdie in golf enthralling duke on Scottish island (9)

indicators.note: holding captive: GOLF holds D
in a down clue, placed on top of the next part

blocks.note: the word itself, split round the duke
D is the abbreviation for duke
inch is a Scottish word for a small island

annotation.surface: A birdie scored at golf in front of a duke on a Scottish island course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Birdie' is the golf score in the surface but a small bird for the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Birdie is a child's word for a little bird, and a goldfinch is one.

entries.clue: That man’s leaving this pub with unknown Aussie beer (5)

indicators.note: HIS leaves the phrase THIS INN

blocks.note: THIS INN, an inn being a pub, with HIS taken out
that man's = HIS, the letters removed
y is an unknown in algebra

annotation.surface: A man walking out of the pub, leaving behind some unfamiliar Australian beer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That man's' is the possessive HIS, lifted from inside 'this inn'.
annotation.definitionFit: Australian slang: beer comes in a tin can, hence the name for the can itself.

entries.clue: Involved, ideally, in hedging? (9)

indicators.note: twisted together: the letters are mixed

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A question about being ideally involved in hedging one's bets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hedging' suggests cautious betting; here it is literal garden hedges. Leylandii are fast-growing conifers notorious in British suburbs for neighbour disputes.
annotation.definitionFit: Leylandii are cypress trees planted in rows as quick-growing hedging.

entries.clue: Keeling over, naked and exhausted (3,2)

indicators.note: stripped of its outer covering: first and last letters go

blocks.note: keeling over = falling; 'naked' then strips off the F and the G

annotation.surface: Someone collapsing, undressed and worn out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Keeling over' supplies a word, FALLING, and 'naked' strips its first and last letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal idiom: someone who has put everything in has nothing left, so is worn out.

entries.clue: Dog days with vacuous little clot (6)

indicators.note: empty: LITTLE loses its middle letters

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
d = days, a standard abbreviation
LITTLE emptied to its outer letters

annotation.surface: The dog days of summer spent with a brainless little idiot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clot' looks like the noun for a fool, fitting 'vacuous'; it is the verb to thicken.
annotation.definitionFit: Milk that curdles clots into lumps.

entries.clue: Just catching heartless robber while active (2,3,3)

indicators.note: ONLY catches and holds the robber
the middle letter is removed

blocks.note: just = only; it wraps round THEF
THIEF without its central I

annotation.surface: Police just managing to nab a callous robber while he is on the move.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' suggests cruelty; it means the robber loses his middle letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Doing something on the fly means doing it while in motion or busy with something else.

entries.clue: Finally goes bald, untroubled (10)

indicators.note: take the final letter of the next word

blocks.note: the last letter of GOES
without tresses, i.e. hairless

annotation.surface: Someone who ends up going bald and is untroubled by it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bald' is not a synonym hunt for HAIRLESS but TRESSLESS, without tresses, which leaves room for the S in front.
annotation.definitionFit: Stressless means free from stress, untroubled.

entries.clue: One expecting male tenor to accept additional honour (6-2-2)

indicators.note: M and T take OTHER in between them

blocks.note: m = male
additional = other, as in 'other costs'
t = tenor, as in SATB
the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

annotation.surface: A tenor looking forward to receiving yet another honour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Expecting' sounds like awaiting an award; it means pregnant.
annotation.definitionFit: A mother-to-be is a pregnant woman, one expecting a baby.

entries.clue: Essentially resetting the whole system is daunting task (4,5)

indicators.note: at its essence, its centre: the middle letter

blocks.note: the middle letter of RESETTING
the whole = all
a system = an order, an arrangement

annotation.surface: An IT worker's lament: rebooting the entire system is a big job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' seems to be an adverb qualifying the sentence; it points at the heart of 'resetting'.
annotation.definitionFit: A tall order is a request that is hard to fulfil.

entries.clue: Spell “carpets” backwards (4)

indicators.note: read the word from the end

blocks.note: to carpet someone is to reprimand them; to pan is to criticise harshly

annotation.surface: An instruction to spell the word carpets in reverse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spell' pretends to mean spelling out letters; it is the noun, as in a cold snap. Carpet is British slang for tell off.
annotation.definitionFit: A snap is a brief spell of weather, as in a cold snap.

entries.clue: Spin sanctimonious contents of proud letter (9)

indicators.note: what is inside: the words minus their first and last letters

blocks.note: pi is informal for pious, sanctimonious
PROUD without its outer letters
LETTER without its outer letters

annotation.surface: Spin doctors wrapping a pious message inside an arrogant letter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contents of' covers both words that follow: each gives up its inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the ballet dancer's full turn on one foot is a kind of spin.

entries.clue: Did up front of shoe, covered in grass (8)

indicators.note: wrapped inside another word

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass; it covers VAMP
the vamp is the upper front part of a shoe

annotation.surface: Doing up a shoe whose toe got covered in grass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Front of shoe' looks like an instruction to take the letter S; it is the vamp, a shoemaker's word.
annotation.definitionFit: To revamp is to renovate, so revamped means did up.

entries.clue: Invalid name for hotel in Yorkshire port (4)

indicators.note: in place of: N stands in for H

blocks.note: Hull is a port city in East Yorkshire
n = name
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet; it is replaced

annotation.surface: A hotel in a Yorkshire port registered under an invalid name.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hotel' looks like a building in the port; it is the letter H, which N replaces in HULL, the port city on the Humber.
annotation.definitionFit: A null contract or vote is void, invalid.

entries.clue: Ring, if declared leader (10)

indicators.note: said out loud: the word for 'if' as it sounds

blocks.note: to ring = to bell, give someone a call
if = whether, which sounds like wether, a castrated ram

annotation.surface: Ring me, if you are declared the winner.
annotation.walkthrough: A bellwether is the wether wearing a bell that leads the flock, so the word means a leader or trendsetter.
annotation.definitionFit: A bellwether is the leading sheep, and by extension anything that leads or indicates a trend.

entries.clue: Superannuated fool, retired flyer (4,2)

indicators.note: gone back: the fool reads backwards

blocks.note: a sap is a gullible fool; turned back it gives PAS
a tit is a small bird, which reads the same either way

annotation.surface: A description of an aged, foolish retired pilot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' suggests a pilot, fitting 'retired'; it is a bird. TIT is a palindrome, so 'retired' works on the pair.
annotation.definitionFit: Past it means too old to do something well, superannuated.

entries.clue: Expert reindeer herders reportedly falling out (8)

indicators.note: as it is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: a pro = a professional, an expert
the Lapps (Sami) of northern Scandinavia herd reindeer

annotation.surface: Skilled reindeer herders said to have fallen out with each other.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Falling out' looks like a quarrel; here it is medical, an organ slipping out of place.
annotation.definitionFit: A prolapse is the slipping or falling out of an organ from its normal position.

entries.clue: Demonstration of parking on top of building (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, P sits above ROOF

blocks.note: P is the parking sign
the top of a building is its roof

annotation.surface: Showing off a rooftop car park on a building.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On top of building' seems to describe a roof car park; it places P over ROOF, since the top of a building is the roof.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: showing that something is true is proving it, as in a mathematical demonstration.

entries.clue: Asterix, say, mostly scoffed chops and cake (6)

indicators.note: most of the word but not all of it, so the final letter is dropped
cuts into: ATE splits GAU

blocks.note: Asterix is a GAUL, minus its last letter
scoffed = ate greedily; it chops GAU in two

annotation.surface: The comic-book Gaul Asterix wolfing down chops followed by cake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chops' reads as meat on Asterix's plate; it is the verb, cutting GAU apart.
annotation.definitionFit: French for cake, borrowed into English for a rich, cream-filled one.

entries.clue: Hostile force failing to end a purge (5)

indicators.note: doesn't reach its end: the last letter goes

blocks.note: the enemy is a hostile force; minus the Y
the word itself

annotation.surface: A hostile army unable to complete a purge of its ranks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Purge' sounds political; here it is bodily.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: flushing liquid into the bowel purges it.

entries.clue: Naughty extract from Lawrence Durrell withdrawn (4)

indicators.note: a piece taken from the words that follow
drawn back: the piece reads backwards

blocks.note: the letters span the end of LAWRENCE and the start of DURRELL

annotation.surface: A racy passage from a Lawrence Durrell novel that was pulled from publication.
annotation.walkthrough: Lawrence Durrell was a British novelist, and the surface trades on literary censorship; the answer runs backwards across the join of his two names.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the smutty sense: a joke that is rude is a naughty one.

entries.clue: Snatch of recondite rumour (2,3)

indicators.note: a snatch is a small piece taken from the word

blocks.note: recONDITe

annotation.surface: Overhearing a fragment of some obscure gossip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recondite' (obscure) looks like it belongs to the definition; it only houses the answer, a French phrase used in English.
annotation.definitionFit: An on dit (French, 'they say') is a piece of gossip, a rumour.

entries.clue: Kit of crack soldiers within Egypt’s borders (9)

indicators.note: means inside, so QUIP and MEN sit inside the other letters
a country's borders are its edges, so only the outer letters of EGYPT count

blocks.note: the first and last letters of EGYPT, which hold the rest
a crack = a wisecrack, a quip
soldiers = men

annotation.surface: The gear carried by elite troops stationed on Egypt's frontiers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crack soldiers' reads as elite troops; 'crack' is split off as a joke, a quip.
annotation.definitionFit: Kit is equipment, the gear needed for a job.

entries.clue: Indication of a setter going mad (9)

indicators.note: the letters behave wildly and rearrange

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A sign that the crossword setter is losing their mind.
annotation.walkthrough: The self-mocking surface about the setter hides the fodder 'of a setter' in plain view.
annotation.definitionFit: A foretaste is an early indication of what is to come.

entries.clue: Close to Blackbeard, degenerate buccaneer (5)

indicators.note: the close, the end, of the word

blocks.note: the last letter of BLACKBEARD
a rake is a dissolute, degenerate man

annotation.surface: A description of a depraved pirate who sailed near Blackbeard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close to' seems to mean near Blackbeard; it means the last letter of his name. Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan privateer.
annotation.definitionFit: Francis Drake was a privateer, a licensed buccaneer, raiding Spanish ships.
